# Passage

> Turn your AI chats into links you’ll be proud to share.

Passage turns public ChatGPT, Codex, and Claude conversations into shareable pages with a concise title, AI-generated highlights, a social preview card, and the saved conversation with its original-source link. No account is required.

## Workflow

1. Paste a public conversation link: `https://chatgpt.com/share/<uuid>`, `https://chatgpt.com/s/cx_<id>`, or `https://claude.ai/share/<uuid>`.
2. Review and edit the generated title, add or remove optional highlights, and choose a card style.
3. Publish the passage and copy its share link. Preparation alone does not publish.

Published wording is fixed. Private conversations are not supported. Known unsupported media, tools, and artifacts are marked as omissions. Confirmed removal of the source disables its existing passages; availability checks are not instantaneous.

## For agents

Install the passage-share skill with the skills CLI:

```sh
npx skills add transitive-bullshit/share-ai-passage --skill passage-share
```

Then ask your agent to use passage-share with a public conversation URL. Requires Node.js 24+. The bundled CLI uses https://www.share-ai-passage.com by default; no checkout or local service is needed. It prepares a preview and publishes when authorized. Keep draft tokens private.

## Links

- [Create a passage](https://www.share-ai-passage.com/): Browser creation workflow.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/share-ai-passage): MIT-licensed application.
- [CLI and setup](https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/share-ai-passage/blob/main/contributing.md): Local setup, configuration, and prepare/publish commands.
- [Agent skill](https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/share-ai-passage/blob/main/.agents/skills/passage-share/SKILL.md): Share an existing public conversation using the bundled CLI. Override PASSAGE_URL only for a self-hosted or development service.
- [Product behavior](https://github.com/transitive-bullshit/share-ai-passage/blob/main/docs/MVP_PLAN.md): Supported behavior, limits, and scope.
